content: Payments API database connection exhaustion occurred during a traffic spike. The incident was associated with a misconfigured application connection pool. Reducing the application connection pool size and recycling affected application pods resolved the incident.
Root cause for INC-2026-0918: the number of retained database connections per application instance exceeded available database capacity.
Engineering successfully inspected PostgreSQL active connections to confirm connection exhaustion during incident INC-2026-0918.
Reducing the application connection pool size and recycling affected application pods resolved incident INC-2026-0918.
After remediation during INC-2026-0918, database connection usage dropped below 60% and Payments API 5xx errors returned to baseline.
An attempt to increase database max_connections immediately during incident INC-2026-0918 failed because database capacity could not be safely increased without broader infrastructure changes.
Checkout latency increased because of payment dependency timeouts during transient load. Investigation identified downstream payment saturation as the important failure condition.
An attempt to increase the checkout request timeout during INC-2026-0922 failed because it increased queued requests without resolving downstream payment saturation.
Reducing retry amplification and restoring payment capacity resolved the checkout incident. Downstream saturation decreased and checkout latency recovered.

Before modifying database capacity, check recent deployment or configuration changes and validate application connection-pool behavior. Avoid increasing database limits without confirming infrastructure capacity.
